name: Professor Glitch
positioning: First-principles mindset for non-tech: Uses everyday analogies to clearly separate automation, AI agents, and digital workers; emphasizes fixing workflows before adding AI.

name: IBM Technology
positioning: Enterprise architecture & standards: Uses lightboard sketches to show how to assemble AI agents into safe, secure, enterprise-grade digital worker systems.

name: AI Explained
positioning: Realistic AI capability testing: Relies on research papers to objectively pinpoint what AI agents can actually do vs. where they hallucinate, completely hype-free.

name: Fireship
positioning: Bite-sized core concepts: Breaks down emerging tech and AI agents in 2-3-minute fast-paced, satirical videos tailored for developers.

name: Centelli
positioning: Business operations & ROI: Shows how to pair traditional RPA bots with AI to handle accounting and paperwork, cutting real-world operational costs.

name: Michele Torti
positioning: Visual workflows for non-coders: Uses drag-and-drop tools (n8n, Make) to connect rigid automations and AI agents into smooth end-to-end routines.

name: Tech With Tim
positioning: Hands-on agent coding: Live-codes in Python step-by-step to show how to build an AI agent from the ground up.
